﴿And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him﴾ — i.e., whoever trusts in Allah regarding what befalls him, He suffices him in what concerns him.

﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ — al-Jumhur read "bālighun amrahu" with tanwin on "bālighun" and nasb on "amrahu." Hafs read it with the idafah (construct). Ibn Abi ʿAblah, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and Abu ʿAmr in one narration from him read it with tanwin on "bālighun" and raf on "amruhu," either as the subject of "bālighun," or as "amruhu" being a postponed subject and "bālighun" a preceding predicate.

Al-Farraʾ, in explaining this reading, said: his command is attaining. The meaning according to the first and second readings is that Allah, glorified is He, attains whatever He wills of the command; nothing escapes Him and no objective is beyond His power. According to the second reading, it means that Allah's command is executed and nothing turns it back.

Al-Mufaddal read "bālighan" in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and the predicate of "inna" is His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah has set a measure for everything﴾ — i.e., a determination, a timing, or an amount.

He, glorified is He, has set for hardship a term at which it ends, and for ease a term at which it ends.

Al-Suddi said: this refers to the measure of menstruation and the ʿiddah.

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation — if you are in doubt﴾ — they are the elderly women whose menstruation has ceased and who have despaired of it — ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ — i.e., you are uncertain and do not know what their ʿiddah is — ﴿then their ʿiddah is three months.﴾

﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾ — because of their youth and because they have not reached the age of menstruation.

I.e., their ʿiddah is three months; this has been omitted because what precedes it indicates it.

﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is that they give birth to their burden﴾ — i.e., the end of their ʿiddah is the delivery of the child. The apparent meaning of the verse is that the ʿiddah of pregnant women is by delivery, whether they are divorced or widowed. This matter has already been discussed fully in Surat al-Baqarah, and we have investigated it in this verse and in the other verse: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

It was also said: the meaning of "if you are in doubt" is "if you are certain." Ibn Jarir preferred that it means doubt, and this is the apparent sense.

Al-Zajjaj said: "if you are in doubt" about her menstruation, when menstruation has ceased for her and she is of the type who menstruates.

Mujahid said: "if you are in doubt" means you do not know the ʿiddah of the one who has despaired and of the one who has not menstruated; the ʿiddah is this.

It was also said: the meaning is "if you are in doubt about the blood that appears from her, whether it is menstruation or not, but rather istihadah (irregular bleeding)" — then the ʿiddah is three months.

﴿And whoever fears Allah — He will make for him of his affair ease﴾ — i.e., whoever guards against Him in obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, He will make easy his affair in this world and the Hereafter.

Al-Dahhak said: whoever fears Allah, let him divorce according to the Sunnah; He will make for him of his affair ease in the return.

Muqatil said: whoever fears Allah by avoiding His disobedience, He will make for him of his affair ease in granting him success in obedience.

The reference in His saying "that" is to the rulings mentioned; that is, that mentioned of the rulings — ﴿is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you﴾ — i.e., His judgment by which He judges among His servants, and His law which He has legislated for them. The meaning of ﴿which He has sent down to you﴾ is that He sent it down in His Book upon His Messenger, explained it to you, detailed its rulings, and clarified its lawful and unlawful.

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ — by abandoning what He does not approve — ﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾ — which he has committed — because piety is among the causes of forgiveness of sins — ﴿and will magnify for him a reward﴾ — i.e., He will give him in the Hereafter a great reward, which is Paradise.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divorced Hafsah, and she went to her family. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾, and it was said to him: Take her back, for she is one who fasts much and stands in prayer much, and she is among your wives in Paradise."

Ibn Jarir reported it from Qatadah as mursal (with a missing companion in the chain).

Al-Hakim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "ʿAbd Yazid, Abu Rukanah, divorced Umm Rukanah, then married a woman from Muzaynah, and she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, she gives me nothing more than this hair does for a hair — she took a hair from her head. At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was seized with zeal. He called Rukanah and his brothers, then said to his companions: Do you see such-and-such from such-and-such? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿAbd Yazid: Divorce her, and he did. He said to Abu Rukanah: Take her back. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I have divorced her. He said: I know that; take her back. Then this was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾."

Al-Dhahabi said: its chain is weak (wahin), and the report is erroneous, for ʿAbd Yazid did not live to see Islam.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Umar that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry, then said: "Let him take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates and becomes pure again. Then if he wishes to divorce her, let him divorce her while she is pure, before he has intercourse with her. That is the waiting period (iddah) which Allah commanded for women to be divorced in." And the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period" [65:1].

Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period."

Ibn al-Anbari narrated from Ibn Umar that he recited: "divorce them for the commencement of their waiting period."

Ibn al-Anbari, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Mujahid that he recited it likewise.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Ubayd in his Fada'il, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he recited it likewise.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Whoever wishes to divorce in accordance with the Sunnah, as Allah has commanded him, let him divorce her while she is pure, without having had intercourse with her."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿So divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [65:1] that he said: "While they are pure, without intercourse." And there are hadiths on this topic.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿And count the waiting period﴾ [65:1] that he said: "Divorce while she is pure, without intercourse."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Umar regarding His words: ﴿And they shall not leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ [65:1] that he said: "Her leaving her house before the end of the waiting period is the clear immorality."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ that he said: "It is adultery."

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The clear immorality is that the woman mistreats the family of the man with her tongue; when she mistreats them verbally, it becomes lawful for them to expel her."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Fatimah bint Qays regarding His words: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ [65:1] that she said: "It is the reconciliation (raj'ah)."

Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Sirin that a man asked Imran ibn Husayn about a man who divorced without calling witnesses. He said: "Evil is what he did. He divorced in an innovated manner and took her back outside the Sunnah. Let him call witnesses to his divorce and to his taking her back, and let him seek forgiveness from Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ [65:2] that he said: "His way out is that he knows that it is from Allah, and that Allah is the One who gives and withholds, who tests him, who grants him well-being, and who repels harm from him." And regarding His words: ﴿and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [65:3] he said: "From where he does not know."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ that he said: "He will save him from every distress in this world and the Hereafter."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, while al-Dhahabi weakened it, narrated through the route of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, who said: "This verse, ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾, was revealed concerning a man from the tribe of Ashja' who was poor, had little means, and had many dependents. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: 'Fear Allah and be patient.' He did not remain long before his son came to him with sheep which the enemy had seized. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), asked him about them and informed him of their matter. He said: 'Eat them.' Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾..."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my son has been captured by the enemy and his mother is distressed. What do you command me?' He said: 'I command you and her to increase your saying: There is no power and no strength except with Allah.' The woman said: 'What a good thing he has commanded you!' So they both increased in saying it. The enemy became careless about him, so he drove off their sheep and brought them to his father. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾..."

There are narrations in this regard that support this.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Aishah regarding the verse that she said: "He is sufficed for the worry and distress of this world."

Ahmad, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Dharr who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept reciting this verse: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ ﴿and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, repeating it until I became drowsy. Then he said: 'O Abu Dharr, if all the people took hold of it, it would suffice them.'" And there are hadiths on this topic.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [65:3] that he said: "The one who relies upon Allah is not the one who says: 'My need is fulfilled.' Not everyone who relies upon Allah is one whom He suffices for what concerns him, repels from him what he dislikes, and fulfills his need. Rather, Allah has made the excellence of one who relies upon Him over one who does not rely upon Him that He expiates his misdeeds for him and magnifies his reward." And regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ [65:3] he said: "It means: the decider of His command over the one who relies upon Him and over the one who does not. But the one who relies upon Him has his misdeeds expiated and his reward magnified." And regarding His words: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾ [65:3] he said: "It means a term and an end to which it reaches."

Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya'la, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you relied upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, you would be provided for as the bird is provided for: it goes out hungry in the morning and returns full in the evening."

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that when some people of Madinah heard the revelation of this verse in al-Baqarah concerning the waiting period of women, they said: "There remain among the waiting periods of women some that are not mentioned in the Qur'an: the young and the old who have ceased menstruating, and women who are pregnant." So Allah revealed: ﴿And those who have despaired of menstruation among your women...﴾ [65:4].

Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Musnad, Abu Ya'la, al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "I said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And for those with pregnancy, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ [65:4]. Is this about the woman divorced three times, or the widow?" He said: "It is about the woman divorced three times and the widow."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daraqutni narrated a similar report from him, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), through another route.

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud that it reached him that Ali said: "She observes the longer of the two waiting periods." Ibn Mas'ud said: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse against him: the verse in Surat al-Nisa' al-Qusra (the shorter one) was revealed after Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And for those with pregnancy, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ [65:4], for so many months. Every divorced woman or widow whose husband has died, her term is until she gives birth to her load."

Similar reports from him were narrated through several routes, and some of them are in Sahih al-Bukhari.

It is established in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Umm Salamah that "Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah's husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth forty nights after his death. She was then proposed to, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her to a man."

There are hadiths on this topic.

This surah is Madani; al-Qurtubi said: "by the consensus of all."

Ibn al-Duraysi, Ibn al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Surat al-Talaq was revealed in Medina."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ — He called the Prophet (ﷺ) first, as an honour to him, then addressed him together with his community; or the address is to him alone, and the plural is for glorification. His community is his model in this matter. The meaning: when you intend to divorce them and have resolved upon it, then divorce them for their ʿiddah, i.e., at the beginning of their ʿiddah, or towards their ʿiddah, or at the time of their ʿiddah.

Al-Jurjani said: the lam in "li-ʿiddatihinna" (for their ʿiddah) has the sense of fi (in), i.e., in their ʿiddah.

Abu Hayyan said: it is by omission of a noun, i.e., for the commencement of their ʿiddah; the lam here indicates timing, like the saying "I met him for a night that remained of such-and-such a month." The intended meaning is that they should divorce them in a tuhr (state of purity) in which there has been no intercourse, and then leave them until their ʿiddah ends. When they divorce them in this way, they have divorced them for their ʿiddah. The explanation of this from the Sunnah will come at the end of the discussion, God willing.

﴿And reckon the ʿiddah﴾ — i.e., keep count of it, and remember the time at which the divorce took place, until the ʿiddah is complete, which is three qurʾ (menstrual cycles/purities). The address is to the husbands; it was said to be to the wives, and it was said to be to the Muslims in general. The first is preferable, because all the pronouns are for them.

﴿And fear Allah, your Lord﴾ — so do not disobey Him in what He has commanded you.

﴿And do not turn them out of their houses﴾ — do not expel them from their homes, i.e., those in which they were at the time of divorce, for as long as they are in the ʿiddah. He attributed the houses to them, though they belong to their husbands, to emphasise the prohibition and to show the full right they have to residence during the ʿiddah. A similar usage is His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34], and His saying: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. Then, having forbidden the husbands to expel them from the houses in which the divorce took place and in which they were residing, He also forbade the wives from going out, saying: ﴿nor let them go out﴾, i.e., they should not go out of those houses for as long as they are in the ʿiddah, except for a necessary matter, as the explanation of that will come. It was also said: the meaning is that they should not leave of their own accord unless the husbands permit them, and then there is no harm. The first is preferable.

﴿Unless they commit a manifest immorality﴾ — this exception belongs to the first clause, i.e., "do not expel them from their houses," not to the second clause.

Al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes hold that the fahishah (immorality) here means fornication, such that she commits zina and is taken out to have the hadd (prescribed punishment) carried out upon her.

Al-Shafiʿi and others said: it means foul speech on the tongue and abusing those who share the house with her. This is supported by what ʿIkrimah said: in the codex of Ubayy there is "unless they behave immorally towards you." It was also said: the meaning is "unless they go out transgressively," for their going out in this manner is an immorality, but this is remote.

The reference in His saying "And these" is to the rulings mentioned; it is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿are the limits of Allah﴾. The meaning is that these rulings which He has explained to His servants are His limits which He has set for them; it is not lawful for them to exceed them to other things.

﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah﴾ — i.e., goes beyond them to other things, or violates any part of them — ﴿has certainly wronged himself﴾ — by bringing himself to the place of ruin and placing himself in the positions of harm, through Allah's punishment upon him for overstepping His limits and transgressing His boundaries.

The clause ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ is an independent clause (mustaʾnafah) establishing the content of what precedes it and giving its reason.

Al-Qurtubi said: all the exegetes said that the "matter" here refers to a desire for reconciliation (ruj'ah); the meaning is an exhortation to divorce only once and a prohibition against divorcing three times, for if one divorces three times he harms himself, when he later regrets the separation and desires to take her back, and finds no way to return to her.

Muqatil said: "after that" means after one or two divorces, a matter that prompts the return.

Al-Wahidi said: the matter that occurs is that love for her return is placed in the man's heart after the first or second divorce.

Al-Zajjaj said: if he divorces her three times at one time, there is no sense in His saying: ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾.

﴿Then when they reach their term﴾ — i.e., they approach the end of the ʿiddah term and near its conclusion — ﴿then retain them in kindness﴾ — i.e., take them back with good companionship and a desire for them, without intending harm to them — ﴿or part from them in kindness﴾ — i.e., leave them until their ʿiddah ends, so that they regain control over themselves, while you fulfil what is due to them from you in rights and refrain from harming them.

﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾ — over the return; it was also said: over the divorce; and it was said: over both, to cut off dispute and close the door to contention. The command is for recommendation (nadb), as in His saying: ﴿And call witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾. It was also said that it is for obligation, and al-Shafiʿi held this, saying: witnessing is obligatory in the return and recommended in the separation. Ahmad ibn Hanbal also held this.

In one opinion of al-Shafiʿi, the return does not require witnesses, like other rights; something similar is reported from Abu Hanifah and Ahmad.

﴿And establish the testimony for Allah﴾ — this is a command to the witnesses to give what they have witnessed, seeking nearness to Allah. Its explanation has already been given in Surat al-Baqarah. It was also said: the command is to the husbands to establish the testimony, i.e., the witnesses at the return; so His saying "and call to witness two just men" is a command to the act of witnessing itself, and His saying "and establish the testimony" is a command that it be sincerely for Allah.

The reference in His saying "that" is to what preceded of the command to call witnesses and establish testimony for Allah. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿is what is admonished thereby to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day are singled out because they are the ones who benefit from it, not others.

﴿And whoever fears Allah — He will make for him a way out﴾ — i.e., whoever guards against the punishment of Allah by obeying His commands, avoiding His prohibitions, and standing at His limits which He set for His servants, not overstepping them — He will make for him a way out of the hardships and trials into which he has fallen.

﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ — i.e., from a direction that does not occur to his mind and is not in his reckoning.

Al-Shaʿbi and al-Dahhak said: this applies to divorce specifically; whoever divorces as Allah commanded will have a way out through return within the ʿiddah, and he will be as one of the suitors after the ʿiddah.

Al-Kalbi said: whoever fears Allah by patience at calamity — He will make for him a way out from the Fire to Paradise.

Al-Hasan said: a way out from what Allah has forbidden.

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: a way out from every matter that is straitened for people.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: whoever fears Allah in performing the obligatory duties — He will make for him a way out from punishment and grant him reward from where he does not expect, i.e., He will bless him in what He has given him.

Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah said: whoever fears Allah in following the Sunnah — He will make for him a way out from the punishment of the people of innovation, and grant him Paradise from where he does not expect. Other interpretations have also been given.

The apparent sense of the verse is general, and there is no basis for restricting it to a particular type; what the context concerns enters it as a primary inclusion.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him﴾ — i.e., whoever trusts in Allah regarding what befalls him, He suffices him in what concerns him.

﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ — al-Jumhur read "bālighun amrahu" with tanwin on "bālighun" and nasb on "amrahu." Hafs read it with the idafah (construct). Ibn Abi ʿAblah, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and Abu ʿAmr in one narration from him read it with tanwin on "bālighun" and raf on "amruhu," either as the subject of "bālighun," or as "amruhu" being a postponed subject and "bālighun" a preceding predicate.

Al-Farraʾ, in explaining this reading, said: his command is attaining. The meaning according to the first and second readings is that Allah, glorified is He, attains whatever He wills of the command; nothing escapes Him and no objective is beyond His power. According to the second reading, it means that Allah's command is executed and nothing turns it back.

Al-Mufaddal read "bālighan" in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and the predicate of "inna" is His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah has set a measure for everything﴾ — i.e., a determination, a timing, or an amount.

He, glorified is He, has set for hardship a term at which it ends, and for ease a term at which it ends.

Al-Suddi said: this refers to the measure of menstruation and the ʿiddah.

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation — if you are in doubt﴾ — they are the elderly women whose menstruation has ceased and who have despaired of it — ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ — i.e., you are uncertain and do not know what their ʿiddah is — ﴿then their ʿiddah is three months.﴾

﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾ — because of their youth and because they have not reached the age of menstruation.

I.e., their ʿiddah is three months; this has been omitted because what precedes it indicates it.

﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is that they give birth to their burden﴾ — i.e., the end of their ʿiddah is the delivery of the child. The apparent meaning of the verse is that the ʿiddah of pregnant women is by delivery, whether they are divorced or widowed. This matter has already been discussed fully in Surat al-Baqarah, and we have investigated it in this verse and in the other verse: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

It was also said: the meaning of "if you are in doubt" is "if you are certain." Ibn Jarir preferred that it means doubt, and this is the apparent sense.

Al-Zajjaj said: "if you are in doubt" about her menstruation, when menstruation has ceased for her and she is of the type who menstruates.

Mujahid said: "if you are in doubt" means you do not know the ʿiddah of the one who has despaired and of the one who has not menstruated; the ʿiddah is this.

It was also said: the meaning is "if you are in doubt about the blood that appears from her, whether it is menstruation or not, but rather istihadah (irregular bleeding)" — then the ʿiddah is three months.

﴿And whoever fears Allah — He will make for him of his affair ease﴾ — i.e., whoever guards against Him in obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, He will make easy his affair in this world and the Hereafter.

Al-Dahhak said: whoever fears Allah, let him divorce according to the Sunnah; He will make for him of his affair ease in the return.

Muqatil said: whoever fears Allah by avoiding His disobedience, He will make for him of his affair ease in granting him success in obedience.

The reference in His saying "that" is to the rulings mentioned; that is, that mentioned of the rulings — ﴿is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you﴾ — i.e., His judgment by which He judges among His servants, and His law which He has legislated for them. The meaning of ﴿which He has sent down to you﴾ is that He sent it down in His Book upon His Messenger, explained it to you, detailed its rulings, and clarified its lawful and unlawful.

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ — by abandoning what He does not approve — ﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾ — which he has committed — because piety is among the causes of forgiveness of sins — ﴿and will magnify for him a reward﴾ — i.e., He will give him in the Hereafter a great reward, which is Paradise.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divorced Hafsah, and she went to her family. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾, and it was said to him: Take her back, for she is one who fasts much and stands in prayer much, and she is among your wives in Paradise."

Ibn Jarir reported it from Qatadah as mursal (with a missing companion in the chain).

Al-Hakim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "ʿAbd Yazid, Abu Rukanah, divorced Umm Rukanah, then married a woman from Muzaynah, and she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, she gives me nothing more than this hair does for a hair — she took a hair from her head. At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was seized with zeal. He called Rukanah and his brothers, then said to his companions: Do you see such-and-such from such-and-such? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿAbd Yazid: Divorce her, and he did. He said to Abu Rukanah: Take her back. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I have divorced her. He said: I know that; take her back. Then this was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾."

Al-Dhahabi said: its chain is weak (wahin), and the report is erroneous, for ʿAbd Yazid did not live to see Islam.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Umar that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry, then said: "Let him take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates and becomes pure again. Then if he wishes to divorce her, let him divorce her while she is pure, before he has intercourse with her. That is the waiting period (iddah) which Allah commanded for women to be divorced in." And the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period" [65:1].

Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period."

Ibn al-Anbari narrated from Ibn Umar that he recited: "divorce them for the commencement of their waiting period."

Ibn al-Anbari, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Mujahid that he recited it likewise.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Ubayd in his Fada'il, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he recited it likewise.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Whoever wishes to divorce in accordance with the Sunnah, as Allah has commanded him, let him divorce her while she is pure, without having had intercourse with her."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿So divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [65:1] that he said: "While they are pure, without intercourse." And there are hadiths on this topic.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿And count the waiting period﴾ [65:1] that he said: "Divorce while she is pure, without intercourse."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Umar regarding His words: ﴿And they shall not leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ [65:1] that he said: "Her leaving her house before the end of the waiting period is the clear immorality."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ that he said: "It is adultery."

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The clear immorality is that the woman mistreats the family of the man with her tongue; when she mistreats them verbally, it becomes lawful for them to expel her."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Fatimah bint Qays regarding His words: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ [65:1] that she said: "It is the reconciliation (raj'ah)."

Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Sirin that a man asked Imran ibn Husayn about a man who divorced without calling witnesses. He said: "Evil is what he did. He divorced in an innovated manner and took her back outside the Sunnah. Let him call witnesses to his divorce and to his taking her back, and let him seek forgiveness from Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ [65:2] that he said: "His way out is that he knows that it is from Allah, and that Allah is the One who gives and withholds, who tests him, who grants him well-being, and who repels harm from him." And regarding His words: ﴿and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [65:3] he said: "From where he does not know."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ that he said: "He will save him from every distress in this world and the Hereafter."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, while al-Dhahabi weakened it, narrated through the route of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, who said: "This verse, ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾, was revealed concerning a man from the tribe of Ashja' who was poor, had little means, and had many dependents. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: 'Fear Allah and be patient.' He did not remain long before his son came to him with sheep which the enemy had seized. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), asked him about them and informed him of their matter. He said: 'Eat them.' Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾..."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my son has been captured by the enemy and his mother is distressed. What do you command me?' He said: 'I command you and her to increase your saying: There is no power and no strength except with Allah.' The woman said: 'What a good thing he has commanded you!' So they both increased in saying it. The enemy became careless about him, so he drove off their sheep and brought them to his father. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾..."

There are narrations in this regard that support this.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Aishah regarding the verse that she said: "He is sufficed for the worry and distress of this world."

Ahmad, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Dharr who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept reciting this verse: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ ﴿and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, repeating it until I became drowsy. Then he said: 'O Abu Dharr, if all the people took hold of it, it would suffice them.'" And there are hadiths on this topic.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [65:3] that he said: "The one who relies upon Allah is not the one who says: 'My need is fulfilled.' Not everyone who relies upon Allah is one whom He suffices for what concerns him, repels from him what he dislikes, and fulfills his need. Rather, Allah has made the excellence of one who relies upon Him over one who does not rely upon Him that He expiates his misdeeds for him and magnifies his reward." And regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ [65:3] he said: "It means: the decider of His command over the one who relies upon Him and over the one who does not. But the one who relies upon Him has his misdeeds expiated and his reward magnified." And regarding His words: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾ [65:3] he said: "It means a term and an end to which it reaches."

Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya'la, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you relied upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, you would be provided for as the bird is provided for: it goes out hungry in the morning and returns full in the evening."

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that when some people of Madinah heard the revelation of this verse in al-Baqarah concerning the waiting period of women, they said: "There remain among the waiting periods of women some that are not mentioned in the Qur'an: the young and the old who have ceased menstruating, and women who are pregnant." So Allah revealed: ﴿And those who have despaired of menstruation among your women...﴾ [65:4].

Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Musnad, Abu Ya'la, al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "I said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And for those with pregnancy, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ [65:4]. Is this about the woman divorced three times, or the widow?" He said: "It is about the woman divorced three times and the widow."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daraqutni narrated a similar report from him, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), through another route.

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud that it reached him that Ali said: "She observes the longer of the two waiting periods." Ibn Mas'ud said: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse against him: the verse in Surat al-Nisa' al-Qusra (the shorter one) was revealed after Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And for those with pregnancy, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ [65:4], for so many months. Every divorced woman or widow whose husband has died, her term is until she gives birth to her load."

Similar reports from him were narrated through several routes, and some of them are in Sahih al-Bukhari.

It is established in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Umm Salamah that "Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah's husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth forty nights after his death. She was then proposed to, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her to a man."

There are hadiths on this topic.

This surah is Madani; al-Qurtubi said: "by the consensus of all."

Ibn al-Duraysi, Ibn al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Surat al-Talaq was revealed in Medina."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ — He called the Prophet (ﷺ) first, as an honour to him, then addressed him together with his community; or the address is to him alone, and the plural is for glorification. His community is his model in this matter. The meaning: when you intend to divorce them and have resolved upon it, then divorce them for their ʿiddah, i.e., at the beginning of their ʿiddah, or towards their ʿiddah, or at the time of their ʿiddah.

Al-Jurjani said: the lam in "li-ʿiddatihinna" (for their ʿiddah) has the sense of fi (in), i.e., in their ʿiddah.

Abu Hayyan said: it is by omission of a noun, i.e., for the commencement of their ʿiddah; the lam here indicates timing, like the saying "I met him for a night that remained of such-and-such a month." The intended meaning is that they should divorce them in a tuhr (state of purity) in which there has been no intercourse, and then leave them until their ʿiddah ends. When they divorce them in this way, they have divorced them for their ʿiddah. The explanation of this from the Sunnah will come at the end of the discussion, God willing.

﴿And reckon the ʿiddah﴾ — i.e., keep count of it, and remember the time at which the divorce took place, until the ʿiddah is complete, which is three qurʾ (menstrual cycles/purities). The address is to the husbands; it was said to be to the wives, and it was said to be to the Muslims in general. The first is preferable, because all the pronouns are for them.

﴿And fear Allah, your Lord﴾ — so do not disobey Him in what He has commanded you.

﴿And do not turn them out of their houses﴾ — do not expel them from their homes, i.e., those in which they were at the time of divorce, for as long as they are in the ʿiddah. He attributed the houses to them, though they belong to their husbands, to emphasise the prohibition and to show the full right they have to residence during the ʿiddah. A similar usage is His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34], and His saying: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. Then, having forbidden the husbands to expel them from the houses in which the divorce took place and in which they were residing, He also forbade the wives from going out, saying: ﴿nor let them go out﴾, i.e., they should not go out of those houses for as long as they are in the ʿiddah, except for a necessary matter, as the explanation of that will come. It was also said: the meaning is that they should not leave of their own accord unless the husbands permit them, and then there is no harm. The first is preferable.

﴿Unless they commit a manifest immorality﴾ — this exception belongs to the first clause, i.e., "do not expel them from their houses," not to the second clause.

Al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes hold that the fahishah (immorality) here means fornication, such that she commits zina and is taken out to have the hadd (prescribed punishment) carried out upon her.

Al-Shafiʿi and others said: it means foul speech on the tongue and abusing those who share the house with her. This is supported by what ʿIkrimah said: in the codex of Ubayy there is "unless they behave immorally towards you." It was also said: the meaning is "unless they go out transgressively," for their going out in this manner is an immorality, but this is remote.

The reference in His saying "And these" is to the rulings mentioned; it is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿are the limits of Allah﴾. The meaning is that these rulings which He has explained to His servants are His limits which He has set for them; it is not lawful for them to exceed them to other things.

﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah﴾ — i.e., goes beyond them to other things, or violates any part of them — ﴿has certainly wronged himself﴾ — by bringing himself to the place of ruin and placing himself in the positions of harm, through Allah's punishment upon him for overstepping His limits and transgressing His boundaries.

The clause ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ is an independent clause (mustaʾnafah) establishing the content of what precedes it and giving its reason.

Al-Qurtubi said: all the exegetes said that the "matter" here refers to a desire for reconciliation (ruj'ah); the meaning is an exhortation to divorce only once and a prohibition against divorcing three times, for if one divorces three times he harms himself, when he later regrets the separation and desires to take her back, and finds no way to return to her.

Muqatil said: "after that" means after one or two divorces, a matter that prompts the return.

Al-Wahidi said: the matter that occurs is that love for her return is placed in the man's heart after the first or second divorce.

Al-Zajjaj said: if he divorces her three times at one time, there is no sense in His saying: ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾.

﴿Then when they reach their term﴾ — i.e., they approach the end of the ʿiddah term and near its conclusion — ﴿then retain them in kindness﴾ — i.e., take them back with good companionship and a desire for them, without intending harm to them — ﴿or part from them in kindness﴾ — i.e., leave them until their ʿiddah ends, so that they regain control over themselves, while you fulfil what is due to them from you in rights and refrain from harming them.

﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾ — over the return; it was also said: over the divorce; and it was said: over both, to cut off dispute and close the door to contention. The command is for recommendation (nadb), as in His saying: ﴿And call witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾. It was also said that it is for obligation, and al-Shafiʿi held this, saying: witnessing is obligatory in the return and recommended in the separation. Ahmad ibn Hanbal also held this.

In one opinion of al-Shafiʿi, the return does not require witnesses, like other rights; something similar is reported from Abu Hanifah and Ahmad.

﴿And establish the testimony for Allah﴾ — this is a command to the witnesses to give what they have witnessed, seeking nearness to Allah. Its explanation has already been given in Surat al-Baqarah. It was also said: the command is to the husbands to establish the testimony, i.e., the witnesses at the return; so His saying "and call to witness two just men" is a command to the act of witnessing itself, and His saying "and establish the testimony" is a command that it be sincerely for Allah.

The reference in His saying "that" is to what preceded of the command to call witnesses and establish testimony for Allah. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿is what is admonished thereby to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day are singled out because they are the ones who benefit from it, not others.

﴿And whoever fears Allah — He will make for him a way out﴾ — i.e., whoever guards against the punishment of Allah by obeying His commands, avoiding His prohibitions, and standing at His limits which He set for His servants, not overstepping them — He will make for him a way out of the hardships and trials into which he has fallen.

﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ — i.e., from a direction that does not occur to his mind and is not in his reckoning.

Al-Shaʿbi and al-Dahhak said: this applies to divorce specifically; whoever divorces as Allah commanded will have a way out through return within the ʿiddah, and he will be as one of the suitors after the ʿiddah.

Al-Kalbi said: whoever fears Allah by patience at calamity — He will make for him a way out from the Fire to Paradise.

Al-Hasan said: a way out from what Allah has forbidden.

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: a way out from every matter that is straitened for people.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: whoever fears Allah in performing the obligatory duties — He will make for him a way out from punishment and grant him reward from where he does not expect, i.e., He will bless him in what He has given him.

Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah said: whoever fears Allah in following the Sunnah — He will make for him a way out from the punishment of the people of innovation, and grant him Paradise from where he does not expect. Other interpretations have also been given.

The apparent sense of the verse is general, and there is no basis for restricting it to a particular type; what the context concerns enters it as a primary inclusion.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him﴾ — i.e., whoever trusts in Allah regarding what befalls him, He suffices him in what concerns him.

﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ — al-Jumhur read "bālighun amrahu" with tanwin on "bālighun" and nasb on "amrahu." Hafs read it with the idafah (construct). Ibn Abi ʿAblah, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and Abu ʿAmr in one narration from him read it with tanwin on "bālighun" and raf on "amruhu," either as the subject of "bālighun," or as "amruhu" being a postponed subject and "bālighun" a preceding predicate.

Al-Farraʾ, in explaining this reading, said: his command is attaining. The meaning according to the first and second readings is that Allah, glorified is He, attains whatever He wills of the command; nothing escapes Him and no objective is beyond His power. According to the second reading, it means that Allah's command is executed and nothing turns it back.

Al-Mufaddal read "bālighan" in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and the predicate of "inna" is His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah has set a measure for everything﴾ — i.e., a determination, a timing, or an amount.

He, glorified is He, has set for hardship a term at which it ends, and for ease a term at which it ends.

Al-Suddi said: this refers to the measure of menstruation and the ʿiddah.

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation — if you are in doubt﴾ — they are the elderly women whose menstruation has ceased and who have despaired of it — ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ — i.e., you are uncertain and do not know what their ʿiddah is — ﴿then their ʿiddah is three months.﴾

﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾ — because of their youth and because they have not reached the age of menstruation.

I.e., their ʿiddah is three months; this has been omitted because what precedes it indicates it.

﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is that they give birth to their burden﴾ — i.e., the end of their ʿiddah is the delivery of the child. The apparent meaning of the verse is that the ʿiddah of pregnant women is by delivery, whether they are divorced or widowed. This matter has already been discussed fully in Surat al-Baqarah, and we have investigated it in this verse and in the other verse: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

It was also said: the meaning of "if you are in doubt" is "if you are certain." Ibn Jarir preferred that it means doubt, and this is the apparent sense.

Al-Zajjaj said: "if you are in doubt" about her menstruation, when menstruation has ceased for her and she is of the type who menstruates.

Mujahid said: "if you are in doubt" means you do not know the ʿiddah of the one who has despaired and of the one who has not menstruated; the ʿiddah is this.

It was also said: the meaning is "if you are in doubt about the blood that appears from her, whether it is menstruation or not, but rather istihadah (irregular bleeding)" — then the ʿiddah is three months.

﴿And whoever fears Allah — He will make for him of his affair ease﴾ — i.e., whoever guards against Him in obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, He will make easy his affair in this world and the Hereafter.

Al-Dahhak said: whoever fears Allah, let him divorce according to the Sunnah; He will make for him of his affair ease in the return.

Muqatil said: whoever fears Allah by avoiding His disobedience, He will make for him of his affair ease in granting him success in obedience.

The reference in His saying "that" is to the rulings mentioned; that is, that mentioned of the rulings — ﴿is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you﴾ — i.e., His judgment by which He judges among His servants, and His law which He has legislated for them. The meaning of ﴿which He has sent down to you﴾ is that He sent it down in His Book upon His Messenger, explained it to you, detailed its rulings, and clarified its lawful and unlawful.

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ — by abandoning what He does not approve — ﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾ — which he has committed — because piety is among the causes of forgiveness of sins — ﴿and will magnify for him a reward﴾ — i.e., He will give him in the Hereafter a great reward, which is Paradise.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divorced Hafsah, and she went to her family. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾, and it was said to him: Take her back, for she is one who fasts much and stands in prayer much, and she is among your wives in Paradise."

Ibn Jarir reported it from Qatadah as mursal (with a missing companion in the chain).

Al-Hakim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "ʿAbd Yazid, Abu Rukanah, divorced Umm Rukanah, then married a woman from Muzaynah, and she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, she gives me nothing more than this hair does for a hair — she took a hair from her head. At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was seized with zeal. He called Rukanah and his brothers, then said to his companions: Do you see such-and-such from such-and-such? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿAbd Yazid: Divorce her, and he did. He said to Abu Rukanah: Take her back. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I have divorced her. He said: I know that; take her back. Then this was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾."

Al-Dhahabi said: its chain is weak (wahin), and the report is erroneous, for ʿAbd Yazid did not live to see Islam.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Umar that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry, then said: "Let him take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates and becomes pure again. Then if he wishes to divorce her, let him divorce her while she is pure, before he has intercourse with her. That is the waiting period (iddah) which Allah commanded for women to be divorced in." And the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period" [65:1].

Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period."

Ibn al-Anbari narrated from Ibn Umar that he recited: "divorce them for the commencement of their waiting period."

Ibn al-Anbari, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Mujahid that he recited it likewise.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Ubayd in his Fada'il, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he recited it likewise.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Whoever wishes to divorce in accordance with the Sunnah, as Allah has commanded him, let him divorce her while she is pure, without having had intercourse with her."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿So divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [65:1] that he said: "While they are pure, without intercourse." And there are hadiths on this topic.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿And count the waiting period﴾ [65:1] that he said: "Divorce while she is pure, without intercourse."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Umar regarding His words: ﴿And they shall not leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ [65:1] that he said: "Her leaving her house before the end of the waiting period is the clear immorality."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ that he said: "It is adultery."

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The clear immorality is that the woman mistreats the family of the man with her tongue; when she mistreats them verbally, it becomes lawful for them to expel her."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Fatimah bint Qays regarding His words: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ [65:1] that she said: "It is the reconciliation (raj'ah)."

Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Sirin that a man asked Imran ibn Husayn about a man who divorced without calling witnesses. He said: "Evil is what he did. He divorced in an innovated manner and took her back outside the Sunnah. Let him call witnesses to his divorce and to his taking her back, and let him seek forgiveness from Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ [65:2] that he said: "His way out is that he knows that it is from Allah, and that Allah is the One who gives and withholds, who tests him, who grants him well-being, and who repels harm from him." And regarding His words: ﴿and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [65:3] he said: "From where he does not know."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ that he said: "He will save him from every distress in this world and the Hereafter."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, while al-Dhahabi weakened it, narrated through the route of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, who said: "This verse, ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾, was revealed concerning a man from the tribe of Ashja' who was poor, had little means, and had many dependents. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: 'Fear Allah and be patient.' He did not remain long before his son came to him with sheep which the enemy had seized. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), asked him about them and informed him of their matter. He said: 'Eat them.' Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾..."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my son has been captured by the enemy and his mother is distressed. What do you command me?' He said: 'I command you and her to increase your saying: There is no power and no strength except with Allah.' The woman said: 'What a good thing he has commanded you!' So they both increased in saying it. The enemy became careless about him, so he drove off their sheep and brought them to his father. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾..."

There are narrations in this regard that support this.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Aishah regarding the verse that she said: "He is sufficed for the worry and distress of this world."

Ahmad, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Dharr who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept reciting this verse: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ ﴿and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, repeating it until I became drowsy. Then he said: 'O Abu Dharr, if all the people took hold of it, it would suffice them.'" And there are hadiths on this topic.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [65:3] that he said: "The one who relies upon Allah is not the one who says: 'My need is fulfilled.' Not everyone who relies upon Allah is one whom He suffices for what concerns him, repels from him what he dislikes, and fulfills his need. Rather, Allah has made the excellence of one who relies upon Him over one who does not rely upon Him that He expiates his misdeeds for him and magnifies his reward." And regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ [65:3] he said: "It means: the decider of His command over the one who relies upon Him and over the one who does not. But the one who relies upon Him has his misdeeds expiated and his reward magnified." And regarding His words: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾ [65:3] he said: "It means a term and an end to which it reaches."

Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya'la, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you relied upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, you would be provided for as the bird is provided for: it goes out hungry in the morning and returns full in the evening."

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that when some people of Madinah heard the revelation of this verse in al-Baqarah concerning the waiting period of women, they said: "There remain among the waiting periods of women some that are not mentioned in the Qur'an: the young and the old who have ceased menstruating, and women who are pregnant." So Allah revealed: ﴿And those who have despaired of menstruation among your women...﴾ [65:4].

Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Musnad, Abu Ya'la, al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "I said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And for those with pregnancy, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ [65:4]. Is this about the woman divorced three times, or the widow?" He said: "It is about the woman divorced three times and the widow."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daraqutni narrated a similar report from him, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), through another route.

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud that it reached him that Ali said: "She observes the longer of the two waiting periods." Ibn Mas'ud said: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse against him: the verse in Surat al-Nisa' al-Qusra (the shorter one) was revealed after Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And for those with pregnancy, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ [65:4], for so many months. Every divorced woman or widow whose husband has died, her term is until she gives birth to her load."

Similar reports from him were narrated through several routes, and some of them are in Sahih al-Bukhari.

It is established in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Umm Salamah that "Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah's husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth forty nights after his death. She was then proposed to, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her to a man."

There are hadiths on this topic.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 65, verses 6–7:

His saying ﴿Lodge them where you dwell﴾ is a fresh statement that includes an explanation of what is owed to the women of residence (*sukna*). The word "min" (from) is partitive, meaning: part of the place where you dwell. It was also said that it is superfluous. ﴿According to your means﴾ means according to your wealth and capacity. *Wujd* means ability.

Al-Farra' said: It means according to what one finds. If he is well-off, he expands on her in housing and maintenance (*nafaqa*). If he is poor, then in proportion to that.

Qatada said: If you find nothing but a corner of your house, then lodge her in it.

The scholars differed concerning the woman divorced three times: does she have residence and maintenance or not? Malik and al-Shafi'i held that she has residence but no maintenance.

Abu Hanifa and his companions held that she has both residence and maintenance.

Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr held that she has neither maintenance nor residence. This is the correct view, and I have established it in my commentary on *al-Muntaqa*, in a way that the one who examines it will not need anything else.

﴿And do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾: God, glorified is He, forbade harming them by restricting them in housing and maintenance.

Mujahid said: [It means] in housing.

Muqatil said: [It means] in maintenance.

Abu al-Duha said: It is that he divorces her, and when two days of her waiting period (*iddah*) remain, he takes her back and then divorces her again.

﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth﴾: that is, until the end point, which is their delivery of the child.

There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding the obligation of maintenance and residence for the pregnant divorcee. As for the pregnant widow, Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Shurayh, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Hammad, Ibn Abi Layla, Sufyan and his companions said: she is to be maintained from the entire estate until she gives birth.

Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Jabir ibn Abd Allah, Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Abu Hanifa and his companions said: she is not to be maintained except from her own share. This is the correct view, due to the evidence transmitted on this from the Sunna.

﴿And if they nurse for you﴾ your children after that, ﴿then give them their wages﴾: that is, the wages for their nursing. The meaning is that if divorced women nurse the children of their divorcing husbands from them, then they are owed their wages for that.

﴿And confer among yourselves in kindness﴾: this is addressed to husbands and wives. That is: consult with one another in what is customary and not reprehensible, and let each of you accept from the other what is good and beautiful. The original meaning is: let one of you instruct the other in what is customary among people and not reprehensible in their eyes.

Muqatil said: The meaning is that the father and the mother should agree on a named wage. It was said: The good and beautiful conduct of the husband is that he provide her wage in full, and the good and beautiful conduct of hers is that she not demand from the wage what the husband finds difficult.

﴿And if you are in difficulty﴾, that is, regarding the wage for nursing (p. 1503), and the husband refuses to give the mother the wage, and the mother refuses to nurse him except for what she wants of the wage, ﴿then another woman will nurse for him﴾: that is, he hires another nursing woman to nurse his child. He is not obligated to meet what the wife demands, and it is not permissible for him to compel her to nurse for the wage he desires.

Al-Dahhak said: If the mother refuses to nurse, he hires another for his child. If she does not accept, then his mother is compelled to nurse for the wage.

﴿Let the one of abundance spend from his abundance﴾: this is a command to the wealthy to widen the provision for the nursing women among their women according to the extent of their wealth. ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾: that is, whose provision is at the measure of subsistence, or constricted and not expanded, ﴿let him spend from what God has given him﴾: that is, from the provision God has given him, and he has no obligation beyond that. ﴿God does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾: that is, what He has given it of provision. So the poor man is not burdened to spend what is beyond his capacity; rather, he is obligated to what he is able to do and what his strength reaches, from what God has given him of provision. ﴿God will bring about, after hardship, ease﴾: that is, after constriction and hardship, abundance and wealth.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿according to your means﴾, that he said: according to your wealth. [Regarding] ﴿And do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾, he said: in housing.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him, regarding His saying ﴿And if they are pregnant﴾ up to the verse, that he said: This is about the woman whom her husband divorces while she is pregnant. So God commanded him to lodge her and maintain her until she gives birth, and if she nurses, until she weans [the child]. If he divorces her finally while she is not pregnant, then she has residence until her waiting period ends, but no maintenance.

Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from Abu Sinan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab asked about Abu Ubayda, and it was said: He wears coarse garments and eats the roughest food. So he sent to him a thousand dinars, and said to the messenger: Watch what he does with them when he takes them. He did not wait long before he wore the softest garments and ate the finest food. The messenger came and informed him. He said: May God have mercy on him; he interpreted this verse: ﴿Let the one of abundance spend from his abundance, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what God has given him﴾.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 65, verses 8–12:

When He (glorified is He) mentioned the rulings that had preceded, He warned against opposing them, and He mentioned the defiance of a people who opposed His commands, so His punishment befell them. He said: ﴿And how many a town defied the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾, meaning it disobeyed, and what is meant is its people. The meaning is: how many people of a town disobeyed the command of Allah and His messengers, or turned away from the command of Allah and His messengers, with "defied" (ataat) taken to imply "turned away" (a'radat). We have already discussed "ka'ayyin" (how many) in Surat Al 'Imran and elsewhere. ﴿So We called it to account with a severe reckoning﴾, meaning: We were stringent with its people in the reckoning for what they had done.

Muqatil said: Allah called it to account for its deeds in this world and recompensed it with punishment, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿and We punished it with an awful punishment﴾, meaning We punished its people with a great, unprecedented punishment in the Hereafter. It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, meaning: We punished its people with an awful punishment in this world, by hunger, famine, the sword, being swallowed up by the earth and being transformed, and We called them to account in the Hereafter with a severe reckoning.

And "nukr" means "munkar" (the unprecedented, the abhorrent).

﴿So it tasted the consequence of its affair﴾, meaning the outcome of its disbelief. ﴿And the outcome of its affair was loss﴾, meaning destruction in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment﴾ in the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire, and the repetition is for emphasis. ﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾, meaning O people of sound intellects. His words ﴿who have believed﴾ are in the accusative position by the implied "a'ni" (I mean), as an explanation of the vocative addressed by ﴿O people of understanding﴾, or as an appositive (atf bayan) to it, or as an adjective (na't).

﴿Allah has sent down to you a reminder, [and] a messenger﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the sending down of the reminder is evidence for an implied "arsala" (He sent), meaning: He sent down to you the Qur'an and sent to you a messenger. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: "rasulan" (a messenger) is in the accusative by the verbal noun "dhikran" (a reminder), since a nunated verbal noun governs.

The meaning is: He sent down to you the reminder of the Messenger.

It was also said: "rasulan" is a substitute (badal) for "dhikran", as if he made the Messenger the very reminder, for emphasis.

It was also said: it is a substitute for it with an omitted noun from the first, the estimate being: He sent down one possessing a reminder, a messenger, or a bearer of a reminder, a messenger.

It was also said: "rasulan" is a descriptive (na't) with an omitted noun, i.e., a reminder that is a messenger, so "dha rasulin" (possessing a messenger) is an adjective of the reminder.

It was also said: "rasulan" is in the accusative as an incitement (al-igra'), as if he said: "Adhere to a messenger."

It was also said: the reminder here means honour (al-sharaf), as in His words: ﴿We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder﴾ [al-Anbiya': 10] and His words: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44].

Then He explained this honour, saying: "a messenger." It has been held by most that what is meant by the Messenger here is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Kalbi said: it is Jibril, and what is meant by the reminder is the Qur'an. The meaning varies according to the differing grammatical analyses mentioned above, as is not hidden.

Then He described the aforementioned Messenger, saying: ﴿reciting to you the verses of Allah, clarified﴾, meaning in a state of their being clarifying. The majority read "mubayyinat" in the form of the passive participle, meaning: Allah made them clear and manifest. Ibn 'Amir, Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it in the form of the active participle, meaning the verses clarify for people what they need of the rulings.

Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd preferred the first reading, on account of His words: ﴿We have certainly made clear to you the verses﴾ and ﴿to bring out those who have believed and done righteous deeds from darknesses into light﴾. The lam is connected to "yatlu" (recites), meaning: that the Messenger who recites the verses may bring out those who believed and did righteous deeds from the darknesses of error into the light of guidance. It is also permissible for the lam to be connected to "anzala" (sent down), in which case the one who brings out is Allah (glorified is He).

﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness﴾, meaning who combines affirmation with acting upon what Allah has obligated on him, along with avoiding what He has forbidden. ﴿He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. The majority read "yudkhilhu" with the ya' (third person), while Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with the nun (first person plural). The pronoun in ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ is pluralized in view of the meaning of "man", and it is singularized in ﴿yudkhilhu﴾ in view of its wording. The clause ﴿Allah has certainly perfected for him provision﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "khalidina" by interlacing (al-tadakhul), or from the object of "yudkhilhu" by synonymy (al-taradif). The meaning of ﴿Allah has certainly perfected for him provision﴾ is: He expanded his provision in Paradise.

﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens﴾. The noble Name is the subject, and its predicate is the relative clause with its complement. ﴿And of the earth, the like of them﴾, meaning: and He created of the earth the like of them, that is, seven.

It has been disputed concerning the manner of the layers of the earth.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: "They have been disputed on two views: the first, which is the view of the majority, is that they are seven earths, layered one above another, with a distance between each earth and another like the distance between the heaven and the earth, and in each earth there are inhabitants of Allah's creation."

Al-Dahhak said: they are closed one upon another without gaps, unlike the heavens.

The first is more sound, because the reports indicate it, in al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others, and this has been explained previously in al-Baqarah. He said: In Sahih Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever takes a shibr of the earth unjustly, he will have it hung around his neck on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths," to the end of his words. What will come at the end of the discussion will strengthen the view of the majority.

The majority read "mithlahunna" with the accusative, as a conjunction to "seven heavens", or by an implied verb, meaning: and He created of the earth the like of them.

'Asim, in one transmission from him, read it with the nominative, as a beginning, with the preceding prepositional phrase as its predicate.

﴿The command descends among them﴾: the clause is resumptive, and it may be a description of what precedes it, and "the command" is the revelation.

Mujahid said: the command descends from the seven heavens to the seven earths.

al-Hasan said: between each heaven and the earth.

Qatadah said: in each earth from its earth and each heaven from its heaven there is a creation of His creations, a command of His command, and a decree of His decree. It was also said: "among them" refers to what lies between the lowest earth, which is nearest, and the seventh heaven, which is highest. It was also said: it is what He manages among them of His wondrous management, so He sends down rain, brings forth plants, brings the night and the day, summer and winter, and creates animals of their varied kinds and forms, moving them from state to state.

Ibn Kaysan said: this is the scope and breadth of the language, as it is said of death "the command of Allah," and of wind, clouds and the like.

The majority read ﴿the command descends﴾ from "tanazzul" (descent), with "al-amr" in the nominative as the subject. Abu 'Amr, in one transmission from him, read "yunazzilu" from "inzal" (sending down), with "al-amr" in the accusative as the object, the agent being Allah (glorified is He). The lam in ﴿that you may know that Allah is competent over all things﴾ is connected to "khalaqa" (created), or to "yatanazzalu" (descends), or to an implied element, meaning: He did that so that you might know the perfection of His power and His encompassing of things. This is the meaning of ﴿and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾, so nothing escapes His knowledge, whatever it may be. "'Ilman" (in knowledge) is in the accusative as a verbal noun, since "ahata" (encompassed) means "alima" (knew), or it is a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: He encompassed with an encompassing of knowledge. It may also be a specification (tamyiz).

Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So We called it to account with a severe reckoning﴾, that he said: it means "it was not shown mercy." And regarding ﴿and We punished it with an awful punishment﴾, he said: "great and unprecedented."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from him regarding ﴿Allah has sent down to you a reminder, [and] a messenger﴾ that he said: "Muhammad (ﷺ)."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir reported through Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas that a man said to him: "Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them," to the end of the surah, and Ibn 'Abbas said: "What assures you that I will tell you of it and you will disbelieve?"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab reported through Abu al-Duha from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿and of the earth, the like of them﴾, that he said: "Seven earths, in each earth a prophet like your prophet, and Adam like Adam, Nuh like Nuh, Ibrahim like Ibrahim, and 'Isa like 'Isa."

Al-Bayhaqi said: this is a sound chain, but it is entirely anomalous (shadh bi-marra); I know of no follower for Abu al-Duha in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, reported from Ibn 'Amr, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The earths, between each earth and the one next to it, is a journey of five hundred years, and the uppermost of them is upon the back of a fish whose two ends have met in the heaven, and the fish is upon a rock, and the rock is in the hand of an angel.
